touches.text: The chart chain machines (9.3.2): orient, constrain, survey, decompose, triage, hypothesize, validate, verdict. [Q#98: The verdict's instrument run, and the proofs that exercise it, need bubblewrap, which Windows does not have, so `cairn test --exec` refuses there ("the instance seal is not confirmed ... bubblewrap (bwrap) is not installed") and three teeth stay red on Windows: test_the_instrument_is_run (two teeth) and the standing-verdict-proofs-stay-green check. Measured 2026-11-13. Whether Windows gets its own seal is the per-OS seal question in Q#90 (9.4.2.3.3); this one is the narrow choice that stands beside it: until that is settled, do the bwrap teeth skip on Windows (and read as not-run there), or do they stay red until Windows has a seal of its own?]

Prebuild face: the chart chain, eight machines, each answering one question before a build begins: orient (what is asked, where does it live), constrain (what bounds it), survey (what already exists), decompose (how does it split), triage (what first, by what standard), hypothesize (what do we expect, how would we know we're wrong), validate (what does DONE mean, measured), and after the build, verdict (what done actually meant).

WHY: Law 8: nothing enters proven-space without a proof a hollow build couldn't pass, and the verdict must come from a hand the builder did not guide. A green cannot be self-granted. A machine under CodeMother, not a device: CodeMother does not build, so the tester inside her puts no builder between a build and its verdict, and nothing here needs its own process in the rack, since each proof run is its own process already.
Hollow runs: proves a proof goes red when the build is removed.

Lifetimes. Each tree declares its lifetime when it is made: kept, one activity (eg one sleep run), or until its source file changes. Dropping a tree drops its leaves and its own links. A node goes only when no tree indexes it, so whatever a temporary tree's activity promoted into a permanent tree outlives it. The drop is enforced, not a habit. WHY: a run that ends without dropping its tables leaves them behind forever.
scratch: a proof's throwaway temp dirs and worktrees, cleaned up by the door. WHY: a run must leave nothing behind (4.3.1.7). USERS: the tester.
A device's code lives in cairn/devices/<device>/; its data in ~/.cairn/devices/<device>/<instance>/.
